extracted.intended_audience: users of Singular (computational algebra) working with non-commutative (Weyl / q-Weyl / G-) algebras; mathematicians and developers using the ncfactor.lib, ncpreim.lib, and nctools.lib libraries
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for procedures in Singular's non-commutative libraries (ncfactor.lib, ncpreim.lib, nctools.lib), giving usage, assumptions, return values, purpose, examples, and notes for each routine used in factorization, elimination, preimage, weights and related tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: homogfacNthQWeyl_all: usage and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: homogfacNthQWeyl_all(h); h is a homogeneous polynomial in the n’th q-Weyl algebra with respect to the weight vector [-1,...,-1,1,...,1]. Return: list. Purpose: Computes all factorizations of a homogeneous polynomial h in the n’th q-Weyl algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: returns a list whose elements are lists representing each factorization of the given [-1,...,-1,1,...,1]-homogeneous polynomial. General assumptions: the basering is the nth Weyl algebra with the first n vars representing x1..xn and the second n vars representing d1..dn; n parameters q1,..,qn are given. Example included demonstrating calling homogfacNthQWeyl_all(h) on a constructed ring and polynomial and receiving multiple factorizations in list form.

rubrics_metrics.name: homogfacFirstQWeyl_all: usage and compatibility wrapper
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: homogfacFirstQWeyl_all(h); h is a homogeneous polynomial in the first q-Weyl algebra with respect to the weight vector [-1,1]. Return: list. Purpose: Computes all factorizations of a homogeneous polynomial h with respect to the weight vector [-1,1] in the first q-Weyl algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory / remark: This function is a wrapper for homogfacNthQWeyl_all and exists to maintain downward-compatibility with older versions. Example shows usage on a polynomial in (x,d) with parameter q and lists returned factorizations (as lists).

rubrics_metrics.name: tst_ncfactor: test suite invocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tst_ncfactor(); Purpose: run internal tests for the ncfactor.lib library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outputs progress and 'Successful.' messages for individual internal tests (delete_duplicates_noteval, combinekfinlf, permpp, binarySearch, getAllDivisorsFromFactList, ..., homogfacNthQWeyl_all, ncfactor, etc.). Example: calling tst_ncfactor() prints a sequence of test names each followed by 'Successful.' and finishes with 'All tests ran successfully.' Use to validate library integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: ncpreim.lib purpose (elimination and preimage computations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Library purpose: Non-commutative elimination and preimage computations (ncpreim.lib).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overview: In G-algebras elimination is more involved than in commutative case; not every subset of variables generates an admissible subalgebra, and admissible elimination orderings may not exist. eliminateNC will find an admissible elimination if one exists; preimageNC computes the preimage of an ideal under a homomorphism between G-algebras without requiring the source to be commutative. References and remarks (BGL, GML, Lev) provided. See also kernel procedures (eliminate, preimage) for differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: eliminateNC: usage, assumptions, and behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: eliminateNC(I,v,eng); I ideal, v intvec, eng optional int. Return: ideal — I intersected with the subring defined by the variables not indexed by the entries of v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: entries of v are in 1..nvars(basering) and the corresponding variables generate an admissible subalgebra. Implementation detail: in order to determine the required elimination ordering a linear programming problem is solved with the simplex algorithm. Unlike eliminate (plural), eliminateNC will always find an elimination ordering if one exists. If eng<>0, std is used for Gröbner basis computations; otherwise (default) slimgb is used. printlevel controls debug output (1: progress messages; >=2: all debug messages). Example shows a case where a naive weight is not an elimination weight and eliminateNC will produce an error if attempted with an invalid weight; demonstrates valid elimination weight found.

rubrics_metrics.name: preimageNC: usage, assumptions, and outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: preimageNC(A,f,J[,P,eng]); A ring, f map or ideal, J ideal, P optional string, eng optional int. Assume: f defines a map from A to the basering. Return: nothing (exports an object 'preim' of type ideal to ring A), being the preimage of J under f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: If P is provided and non-empty, the preimage is exported to A under that name; otherwise default name is 'preim'. If eng<>0, std is used for Gröbner basis computations; otherwise default slimgb is used. printlevel controls debug messages. Example: computing preimage (kernel) of a map from U(gl_3) into a Weyl algebra demonstrates resulting ideal elements K[1]=..., K[9]=...; reference (Lev). See also kernel's preimage (plural) documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: admissibleSub: test for admissible subalgebra
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: admissibleSub(v); v intvec. Assume: entries of v are in 1..nvars(basering). Return: int — 1 if the variables indexed by the entries of v form an admissible subalgebra, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: in U(sl_2) with variables e,f,h the subalgebra generated by e,f is not admissible since [e,f]=h (admissibleSub(1..2) -> 0), but the subalgebra generated by f,h is admissible since [f,h]=2f (admissibleSub(2..3) -> 1). Use to check the prerequisite for elimination and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: isUpperTriangular: matrix triangularity check
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isUpperTriangular(M[,k]); M a matrix, k an optional int. Return: int — 1 if M is upper triangular, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: If k<>0 is given, it checks whether M is strictly upper triangular. Example shows a 2x3 matrix with zeros below diagonal returning 1 for both isUpperTriangular(M) and isUpperTriangular(M,1) until a diagonal entry is changed, in which case strict-upper check returns 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: appendWeight2Ord: attach weights to ring ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: appendWeight2Ord(w); w an intvec. Return: ring — the basering equipped with the ordering (a(w),<), where < is the ordering of the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: For a commutative ring appendWeight2Ord returns a ring with specified weights; for a non-commutative ring weights must be chosen to preserve non-commutative relations. After constructing a new weighted ring, activate it with setring. The examples illustrate different 'names'/'weights' and how noncommutative relations remain or change depending on weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: elimWeight: compute elimination weight vector
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: elimWeight(v); v an intvec. Assume: The basering is a G-algebra and entries of v are in 1..nvars(basering) with the corresponding variables generating an admissible subalgebra. Return: intvec w such that the ordering (a(w),<) is an elimination ordering for the subalgebra generated by the variables indexed by v; if no such ordering exists the zero intvec is returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note / Remark: If no elimination ordering exists the zero intvec is returned. Example demonstrates that naive weights (0,0,1,1) may not be elimination weights and elimWeight returns a workable weighting (e.g., 0,0,1,2). References: (BGL), (GML).

rubrics_metrics.name: extendedTensor: build extension ring encoding homomorphism relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: extendedTensor(A,I); A ring, I ideal. Return: ring — A+B (where B denotes the basering) extended with non-commutative relations between the vars of A and B which arise from the homomorphism A -> B induced by I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark / Construction detail: If vars of A are x(i) and vars of B are y(j), compute q(i)(j) = leadcoef(y(j)*I[i]) / leadcoef(I[i]*y(j)) and r(i)(j) = y(j)*I[i] - q(i)(j)*I[i]*y(j); then impose relation y(j)*x(i) = q(i)(j)*x(i)*y(j) + r(i)(j). Example constructs extended tensor of a Weyl and a universal enveloping algebra using an ideal I and prints numerous resulting noncommutative relations. Use when needing a combined ring reflecting imposed relations from a given ideal/homomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gweights: compute weights making relations compatible with weighted ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Gweights(r); r a ring or a square matrix. Return: intvec. Purpose: compute an integer weight vector such that for a G-algebra the relation-leading-monomials satisfy lm w(d_{ij}) < w x_i x_j (i<j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory / notes: Gweights returns an integer vector whose weighting should be used to redefine the G-algebra to get the same non-commutative structure with respect to a weighted ordering. If the input is a matrix and the output is the zero vector then there is no G-algebra structure associated to these relations for the given variables. Example: Gweights(S) -> 2,1,1,1 for a sample algebra. Suggestion: weightedRing can be used as alternative to obtain a G-algebra with appropriate weighted ordering directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: weightedRing: construct ring with weights satisfying G-algebra ordering condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: weightedRing(r); r a ring. Return: ring — the given ring with variable weights chosen such that the relations of the new ring (with weighted variables) satisfy the ordering condition for G-algebras (e.g., for all i<j: lm w(d_{ij}) < w x_i x_j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: equip variables of the given ring with weights so that the relations satisfy the ordering condition for G-algebras. Note: activate the returned ring with setring. Example demonstrates creating weighted ring from an nc_algebra and setting it as active ring. Use when a weighted ordering is required for G-algebra computations.
